newsitem.title: USA: Dry weather seen reducing Argentine soy crop.
newsitem.headline: Dry weather seen reducing Argentine soy crop.

text.p: Recent dry weather in Argentina is seen having an adverse effect on 1997 soybean production, a private U.S. meteorologist said on Saturday at a meeting of the National Institute of Oilseed Products.
"We've got Argentina with a real dearth of moisture at this time," said David Streit, chief agricultural meteorolgist with Cropcast Services in Rockville, Md.
The dry weather prompted Cropcast to lower its 1997 Argentine soybean forecast to 12.4 million tonnes from previous forecasts nearing 13 million tonnes, Streit said.
The dry weather is having the greatest effect on Argentina's later-planted double-crop soybeans, which account for about 25 percent of Argentina's soybean acreage, Streit said.
One Argentine oilseed trader attending the meeting agreed that local weather has not been favourable for the crop, and he estimated the crop at 12.5 million tonnes.
"It's not good," the trader said. "It's not very good at all."
Those estimates are much lower than the U.S. Department of Agriculture's March 1 Argentine soybean production forecast of 13.50 million tonnes.
Weather throughout the soybean growing season and into harvest has been more favourable in Brazil, so harvest there has been running ahead of schedule, Streit told the meeting.
"We are seeing some very high production coming out of Brazil," he said.
Cropcast is forecasting the 1997 Brazilian soybean crop at 26.9 million tonnes, slightly below the USDA's latest forecast of 27 million.
